meeting_header:
Date: 2027-09-14 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58m
Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Priya Nair (CSM)
Customer: Carlos Mendoza (Head of Platform), Nina Patel (SRE), Avery Brooks (Product), Sanjay Rao (Security), Jonah (On-call)
summary: Handover of the operational runbook after the long-tail KV-cache degradation incident. Reviewed telemetry gaps, alert tuning, and an upcoming simulated long-tail error test. Agreed on specific action items: updated fallback orchestration, log extracts, runbook hosting, and a scheduled chaos run. Also discussed encryption/KMS audit traces and SOC2 artifact linkage for post-incident review.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We got a tight agenda — handover of the runbook, go through the sim plan for long-tail errors, and confirm owners.
[00:12] Carlos Mendoza: Yep, thanks. I'm on, I can't stay the full hour but I wanted to make sure the SRE owners are firm.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick intro — Liam's gonna lead the technical bits, Priya on the runbook logistics.
[00:24] Liam O'Connor: Hey, everyone. Quick TL;DR: we're trying to reduce the frequency and impact of those long-tail degraded responses you saw in Feb. We traced a cascade to stale KV cache entries + a subtle retry amplification under the Client lib's backoff.
[00:38] Nina Patel: Right, that's what we saw. Some pods kept holding a stale prefix in their KV, and then when the cache TTL collapsed it caused a flurry of requests to the hot path.
[00:50] Jonah: (background) yeah that was midnight for us — it hit the critical path.
[00:54] Liam O'Connor: And to be clear we also saw a mismatch between request ids in the telemetry and the app logs which slowed triage.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Exactly — that's one of the telemetry gaps we want to close in the runbook handoff.
[01:10] Carlos Mendoza: Can you quickly outline the key sections of the updated runbook? We want to know where to look when something similar starts.
[01:17] Priya Nair: Sure, high level: incident detection triggers, play-by-play for mitigation (circuit breaker flip, cache flush, scaled rollback), postmortem checklist, owners and who to notify, and a simulation plan for rehearsals. Plus a forensic pack (logs, traces) link.
[01:30] Avery Brooks: The simulation plan — how intrusive is it? We can't have a full blackout during peak.
[01:35] Liam O'Connor: The plan is staged. First stage: synthetic traffic to the inference endpoints at low concurrency to validate TTL behavior. Stage two: controlled TTL decay testing where we purposefully reduce cache TTLs on a small canary pool. Stage three: spike and observe fallback orchestration with throttles. All done in off-peak windows and with circuit breakers.
[01:54] Sanjay Rao: From a security perspective we need KMS audit traces and confirmation that the logs are redacted for PII.
[02:00] Priya Nair: We'll attach the SOC2 artifact map to the runbook and include the KMS audit guide. Redwood will export the KMS event set for the relevant timeframe.
[02:09] Maya Chen: Action item: Liam to prepare the orchestration diagram with explicit timeout values — we need those numbers in the runbook.
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: Noted.
[02:18] Nina Patel: One question — during the Feb event there was mention of an 'in-flight' KV cache eviction not propagating. Is that something at the serving runtime level?
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: Short answer: yes, there was a race condition when we trimmed keys on the leader but didn't invalidate the warm caches fast enough on peers — the cold-start path hit heavier kernel routines and caused latency. We've put a mitigation in a patch but we need to rehearse it.
[02:44] Carlos Mendoza: Ok. Will that patch require node restarts? Because we prefer rolling patches with zero-downtime.
[02:51] Liam O'Connor: The patch is a small coordination shim; it can be rolled with a canary then a gradual rollout. We'll outline the rollout steps in the runbook.
[02:59] Maya Chen: Let's talk telemetry: Nina, you said the mismatch — what data do you need us to send?
[03:05] Nina Patel: We need aligned request_id traces (app + gateway) and a short sample of the KV cache key eviction log. Also percentiles on tail latencies (p95/p99) for the offending period.
[03:17] Liam O'Connor: We'll export traces and provide a mapping table. Heads-up: some of the names in the exported traces might be mutated by internal tokens — transcription sometimes mixes up the model names, so double-check the mapping doc.
[03:29] Maya Chen: (laughs) yeah Fireflies sometimes writes "Redwood-serve" as "Redwood swerve" — ignore that.
[03:35] Avery Brooks: Can we also get a simple dashboard query for the TTL and cache hit ratio over time? That would help.
[03:41] Priya Nair: Yes — we'll include Grafana snapshots and the exact PromQL queries.
[03:46] Jonah: On the chaos test scheduling, our ops window is Tue/Wed off-peak 0200-0500 local — can Redwood do that?
[03:53] Maya Chen: We can. Our SEs will be available in a blocking on-call during the run. We'll also provide a rollback checklist.
[03:59] Carlos Mendoza: I'd like to escalate one thing — our legal team wants evidence that this won't create new data retention issues when we run the sim.
[04:07] Sanjay Rao: Specifically, they want assurance that simulated payloads don't get logged in full.
[04:11] Liam O'Connor: We'll run the sim with sanitized payloads and ensure logging is at a level that redacts PII; we'll also document this in the runbook.
[04:18] Nina Patel: Great. On the fallback orchestration — can you show the steps now? Even a quick verbal flow so we understand the order.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: Sure. Step one: detect threshold crossing on tail latency and error rate. Step two: flip circuit to fallback model variant (lower-cost / shorter context) for 10s, then measure. Step three: if errors persist, route to degraded mode (cached responses) and trigger a cache flush job on a per-shard basis. Step four: if still unwell, scale up the dedicated pool and notify engineering channel. Each step has timeouts and an automatic rollout back if error drops below threshold.
[04:55] Carlos Mendoza: The 'cached responses' — are they allowed for legal/regulatory reasons? We cache anonymized responses only?
[05:02] Sanjay Rao: We cache only non-PII. We'll need that documented.
[05:06] Priya Nair: We'll add a small section about allowed cache types and the redaction process.
[05:11] Maya Chen: Ok. For the post-incident forensic pack: Liam will deliver logs and the annotated trace with request id mapping by the 16th. Priya will host the runbook in the shared S3 and give access.
[05:22] Nina Patel: Will there be a test run with our staging environment first? We want to piece it in without touching prod.
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. The rehearsal will be in staging against a realistic workload you provide, then a canary in prod.
[05:34] Avery Brooks: A silly question — do you have a checklist for 'when to open incident bridge vs when to do an async mitigation'? We've had confusion in the past.
[05:43] Maya Chen: We do. The runbook has a decision tree: immediate bridge if tail p99 latency > X and error rate > Y for more than Z minutes and business-impact signals present. Otherwise follow async mitigation steps and monitor. We'll include exact numbers you can tune.
[05:58] Carlos Mendoza: Sounds good. One thing — the Feb RCA mentioned possible request amplification from retries in our client. Do you have explicit guidance for client-side backoff settings?
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: Yes, there's a recommended client config with capped retries and jitter. We'll include an example patch for your client library.
[06:16] Sanjay Rao: For compliance, we also need to tie the runbook to the SOC2 evidence folder and show the timeline we used for the postmortem.
[06:24] Priya Nair: We'll add the artifact links and the timeline.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Ok, let's confirm owners and due dates out loud. Liam — orchestration diagram and logs export by 2027-09-16. Priya — runbook hosting and SOC2 mapping by 2027-09-17. Nina — synthetic workload profile by 2027-09-20. Run chaos sim week of 2027-09-27.
[06:46] Carlos Mendoza: Agreed.
[06:48] Maya Chen: Anything else before we wrap?
[06:51] Avery Brooks: Can Redwood include the quick rollback script in the runbook? That was super helpful last time.
[06:56] Liam O'Connor: We'll push the rollback script and include a one-click command in the doc.
[06:59] Jonah: Thanks.
[07:00] Maya Chen: Ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the simulation.
[07:06] (end)

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels; some names spelled phonetically. Some timestamps approximate.
